column3: Lesson two. A rival can push you, or poison you.
The push is real. Vejeeta became a Super Sayan because of Goku. And in a study of amateur runners, people ran a little faster in races where a rival was also running. That's a link, not proof.

But the same research group found the other side. In seven seasons of Italian football, matches between same-city rivals drew more yellow cards. And in an experiment, students were about four times as likely to lie to someone from their rival university.
That's Vejeeta's darkest moment. Years later, at peace, with a family, he lets a wizard's spell in, on purpose. He attacks a stadium crowd, just to force Goku to fight him.
Researchers describe two kinds of envy. One says, I want to get up there too. The other says, I want them brought down. In small experiments, only the first kind made people work harder.
A rival makes you better while you want to climb. And worse, the moment you'd rather see them fall.
